{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZWrT5g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhC-BgQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 27, "title": "Correct SCU DSP overflow lifetime and arithmetic-status semantics", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17

At main `1edbce3d5ee96747da34461c5635c7a3864cb18a`, `Dsp::alu` preserves the previous V flag and only sets it when another overflow occurs (`src/scu/dsp.rs:274–327`). `Dsp::control` then clears both V and E when reading the program-control port (`src/scu/dsp.rs:105–111`). Consequently, a successful arithmetic operation can report an earlier overflow, while reading status can erase the latest arithmetic result.

These semantics affect general DSP computation and CPU inspection of its results. The current native ALU vectors mostly start with fresh DSP state and inspect status once, so they do not establish correct flag lifetime. The conformance matrix’s claim of read-cleared E/V repeats the implementation and needs correction.

## Expected outcome

Implement and independently verify the SCU DSP arithmetic-status contract:

- ADD, SUB and AD2 replace V with their own signed-overflow result, including clearing it after non-overflowing arithmetic.
- Instructions documented as leaving V unchanged preserve it.
- Program-control reads preserve V while retaining the documented E acknowledgement behavior.
- Results and S/Z/C distinguish 32-bit arithmetic from 48-bit AD2, independently of whether the ALU result is written back to A.

Primary references:

- [Sega SCU DSP Simulator User’s Manual Addendum, ST-240-B-SP1-052295, printed p.5, “Bugs”](https://manualzilla.com/doc/5874469/scu-dsp-assembler-user-s-manual-addendum): explicitly distinguishes actual hardware overflow replacement from the simulator’s sticky-flag defect. The mirror’s page title is incorrect; the document cover identifies the Simulator addendum.
- [Sega Technical Bulletin SOA #8, §3 and §5.1](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/Sattechs.pdf): status-bit definitions, E acknowledgement and instruction flag effects.
- [SCU User’s Manual ST-097-R5, §4.5, ADD/SUB/AD2 and associated transfer instructions](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-097-R5-072694.pdf): arithmetic widths, results and parallel transfers.

Keep the change focused on arithmetic/status semantics and their scheduled guest observability. Additional DMA modes, general pipeline redesign and unrelated rendering changes remain separate work.

## Context and reproduction

Source inspection establishes two distinguishing cases:

1. Execute ADD with A=`7FFFFFFF`, P=`00000001`, writing back the result. Then execute another ADD with P unchanged. The first result is `80000000` with V=1; the second is `80000001` with V=0. Current code retains V=1 after the second operation.
2. Stop after the first overflowing ADD and read program control twice without intervening arithmetic. V must remain set; current code clears it after the first read.

Existing evidence includes `src/scu/tests.rs::dsp_alu_golden_results_carry_sign_zero_and_48_bit_accumulation`, the conditional/control vectors, and the original native/browser SCU and DSP-DMA guests. Preserve these and extend their evidence rather than replacing expectations with captured emulator output.

The supplied snapshot contains no open task Issues, so this does not duplicate an open task. Current main’s build observation is in progress; it is neither failure nor passing evidence. This planning pass used read-only inspection and primary-document research; no tests were rerun.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add independently derived native instruction-program vectors that fail on the inherited implementation for both overflow followed by non-overflowing arithmetic and repeated program-control reads. Cover ADD, SUB and AD2, both overflow directions, unsigned carry/borrow without signed overflow, and zero/sign boundaries. Construct 48-bit operands through documented instructions as well as any focused internal vectors.
- [ ] Correct V replacement, preservation and read behavior. Exercise NOP, logical/shift operations and data transfers between arithmetic operations. Check literal results and S/Z/C/V independently; include parallel ALU-to-memory transfers with and without accumulator writeback. Expected values must not call production arithmetic helpers.
- [ ] Preserve E read acknowledgement, END/ENDI distinction, SCU DSP-end interrupt delivery and guest acknowledgement, pause/single-step behavior, delayed control flow, DMA continuation and existing prohibited-bank diagnostics. Verify that changing V handling neither loses nor duplicates end interrupts.
- [ ] Add an original MIT-licensed SH-2/DSP diagnostic using actual SCU MMIO. Guest instructions upload operands/programs, execute overflowing and subsequent non-overflowing kernels, read halted status repeatedly, consume computed results and record an interrupt-handler result. Include operand mutations, an omitted-arithmetic negative control and repeated cold boots. Host code may load media and inspect records, but must not calculate or write running guest results.
- [ ] Execute identical diagnostic bytes in native Machine tests and production browser Wasm. Compare source-authored result/status records, including the two distinguishing cases above. Native scheduling checks must preserve results across advancement chunks such as 1/3/17/10000, pause/resume and reset, with no stale overflow or end event surviving a cold reset.
- [ ] Record failing inherited-implementation controls and passing corrected results. Make fixture reproduction mandatory in existing CI. Update the conformance matrix to supersede the read-cleared-V claim, cite exact manual sections, link native/browser evidence and retain explicit remaining deviations.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native and Wasm Clippy, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, all fixture/media reproduction checks and the complete existing `npm run test:browser`. Preserve Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, audio, backup, both controller ports, reset behavior and local-file privacy assertions.

This is a partial #17 increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral, multiprocessor/bus/reset, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration requirements remain mandatory. Neither this task nor green CI establishes hardware completion or broad commercial compatibility. Genuine BIOS and commercial-game compatibility remain not independently confirmed. Do not reopen historical trackers or use closing references for #17.

## Optional validation

Additional deterministic arithmetic property vectors using independent wide-integer expectations. No personal firmware, commercial media, physical console, human approval or live Pages inspection is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
